prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1292; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received by phone from the claimant, who reports a low-speed collision while backing out of a space in a parking lot. The claimant states they have no attorney and prefers to handle the claim directly.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of the reported incident. Nothing in the policy history suggests any change in coverage before the loss.

Entry 3: Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm the general location of the impact and the position of the vehicles, though they do not show the moment of contact.

Entry 4: Obtained the responding officer's report, which confirms the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses were identified on the report or during follow-up calls.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle. The damage pattern and location are consistent with the impact described by the claimant, and the estimate was prepared on that basis.

Entry 6: Checked prior claim and damage records for the vehicle. No earlier damage has been recorded, and the claimant has not mentioned any previous incidents.

Entry 7: Spoke with the claimant about the injury. They report a wrist fracture from bracing against the steering wheel. The injury description is in line with the kind of force expected from this type of collision.

Entry 8: Requested medical records. The treating provider documented a wrist fracture and a course of care typical for that injury. No prior injury to the same wrist or arm appears in the records received so far.

Entry 9: Reviewed the treatment timeline. Visits were frequent early on and became less frequent as the claimant's condition improved, which matches the usual recovery pattern for this injury.

Entry 10: Took a recorded follow-up call with the claimant. The account of how the collision happened matched the account given at first notice, including the sequence of events and the location in the lot.

Entry 11: Compared the claimant's statements across all contacts to date, including the phone call, the written statement, and the follow-up call. The account has remained consistent throughout.

Entry 12: Reviewed the file as a whole. The injury, vehicle damage, and driver information all line up with the reported incident, and the claim is proceeding to settlement review pending final medical bills.
